Smallest set of subjects whose removal changes the conclusion

Source: R/fragility.R
stress_fragility.Rd

A greedy forward search: at each step every remaining subject is removed in turn from the current data, the pre-specified model is refitted, and the subject whose removal moves the result furthest towards the target is dropped for good. The search stops when the target is reached or after max_k steps. The number of steps needed is a continuous-outcome analogue of the fragility index; because the search is greedy it is an upper bound on the true minimum.

Usage

stress_fragility(
  spec,
  target = c("significance", "ci", "direction"),
  max_k = 5,
  candidates = NULL,
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

spec

A stress_spec().

target

What has to change: "significance" (the p-value crosses alpha in either direction, depending on the base result), "ci" (the estimate leaves the base confidence interval) or "direction" (the estimate changes sign).

max_k

Maximum number of subjects to remove.

candidates

Optional character vector of subject identifiers to restrict the search to (one arm, say).

cores

Number of worker processes; 1 fits sequentially.

Value

A stress_rows data frame with one row per step (kind = "search", so the rows are not counted in a census, since the search crosses the target by construction; param = number removed, label = the subjects removed so far). attr(, "fragility") is a list with target, k (the step at which the target was reached, NA if never), subjects and reached.

Examples

small <- mmrm::fev_data[mmrm::fev_data$USUBJID %in% paste0("PT", 1:60), ]
spec <- stress_spec(small, "FEV1", "USUBJID", "AVISIT", "ARMCD", "PBO", covariates = ~ FEV1_BL,
                    covariance = "cs", method = "Satterthwaite", vcov = "Asymptotic")
fr <- stress_fragility(spec, max_k = 2)
attr(fr, "fragility")
#> $target
#> [1] "significance"
#> 
#> $k
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $subjects
#> [1] "PT1"
#> 
#> $reached
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $base_p
#> [1] 0.1099548
#> 
#> $base_estimate
#> [1] 3.478182
#>
